rollouts.title: Observation retention and open-loop prediction are distinct tests
rollouts.caption: The same observed pre-reveal context (saved context 2, JEPA model seed 0) and recorded eight-action sequence are used in every row. The context column repeats the last observed RGB frame. Encoded future decodes the JEPA encoding of each true future observation; it is not a prediction. JEPA rollout feeds predicted latents back to the original predictor. Flow shows one stochastic pixel-model rollout. Frames are unmodified RGB arrays with nearest-neighbor display. The frozen decoder is an auxiliary diagnostic and its compute is outside world-model training budgets. This metadata-selected context is an illustration; aggregate evidence uses 64 survival-selected contexts per model seed, with no terminal event in the observed and recorded-future window.
rollouts.selection_rule: first stored context with wall_x=45, selected by environment metadata before inspecting rollout appearance; first predicted frame remains unrevealed

rollouts_full.title: Observation retention and open-loop prediction are distinct tests
rollouts_full.caption: The same observed pre-reveal context (saved context 0, JEPA model seed 0) and recorded eight-action sequence are used in every row. The context column repeats the last observed RGB frame. Encoded future decodes the JEPA encoding of each true future observation; it is not a prediction. JEPA rollout feeds predicted latents back to the original predictor. Flow shows one stochastic pixel-model rollout. Frames are unmodified RGB arrays with nearest-neighbor display. This metadata-selected context is an illustration; aggregate evidence uses 64 survival-selected contexts per model seed, with no terminal event in the observed and recorded-future window. Counterfactual changes only the gap side; head-sample and mean-of-eight rows are distinct residual-head sampling operators.
rollouts_full.selection_rule: first stored context, index 0; no outcome-based selection

control_by_seed.title: Policy outcomes by world-model seed and rollout operator
control_by_seed.caption: Final walls passed per episode in the real gate. Each orange panel is a separately trained JEPA world-model seed; three policy seeds are shown for each operator. Orig. uses the original deterministic predictor; Draw samples its separately trained residual head; Mean8 averages eight head draws. Flow uses one world-model checkpoint, with six sampled-rollout policies and three mean-of-eight policies. Each dot is a policy's final evaluation over 256 episodes. Horizontal bars summarize policies within a model/operator cell; no pooled standard error or inference over world-model seeds is shown. Dashed line is random actions. All trained-model policies receive 1,228,800 imagined transitions. These comparisons do not isolate dynamics from reward heads, observation interfaces, or optimization.

representation_by_seed.title: Direct and decoded latent interfaces under real dynamics
representation_by_seed.caption: Final survival at the 128-step cap, evaluated on 256 episodes per policy after 1,499,136 real environment transitions. Left: MLP policies consume frozen JEPA latents, with a true-pixel MLP reference. Right: CNN policies consume a frozen auxiliary decoder's images, with a true-pixel CNN reference. The three encoder seeds remain separate, with three policy seeds each. Decoder training is outside the world-model budget; decoding tests accessibility through a changed interface, not a compute-matched repair. The dashed 50% threshold is descriptive. No confidence interval is inferred from the policy runs, and the MLP and CNN panels are not an architecture-matched comparison.

geometry_by_seed.title: One-step prediction residual versus encoded obstacle contrast
geometry_by_seed.caption: For each of three independently trained JEPA model seeds, means across 64 reconstructed pre-reveal, survival-selected contexts compare total teacher-forced one-step prediction error with the squared latent distance between the recorded future and a matched future with the wall removed. Distances sum over latent coordinates. Each later one-step prediction is supplied the true context history, so these curves are not open-loop rollout errors. The wall-removal contrast is not a causal attribution of the total residual. Only 40 of the 64 contexts remain unrevealed at the first future step; selection requires no terminal in the observed and recorded-future window. Context-level errors were not retained in the aggregate summary, so no uncertainty band is fabricated. All eight discrete steps are shown; lines connect measurements without smoothing.

evidence_staircase.title: Experimental scope: rich environment, diagnostic obstacle, controlled nuisances
evidence_staircase.caption: Protocol schematic, not a measured performance plot or difficulty ranking. Craftax separates visual goal reaching from reward-based planning; the gate separates information retention, prediction and control around a late-revealed gap; the cube crosses absent, frame-wise and episode-fixed visual noise with still or wind dynamics under survival reward. The current gate uses a white wall, black background and no wind. The six nuisance-cube conditions have no wall. The diagram does not imply that the full nuisance grid was evaluated in the gate.

craftax_summary.title: Craftax visual goal reaching versus reward planning
craftax_summary.caption: Left: fraction matching the goal position in a single six-step open-loop action plan across 128 saved states, with goals generated by random six-action sequences; the simulator reference executes the known recorded action sequence. Right: mean 100-step real-environment return across 128 states with a six-step planning horizon. Random, myopic, greedy and MPC are distinct action-selection procedures. Both panels use one JEPA model checkpoint and are descriptive, without model-seed confidence intervals. They test different objectives and should not be interpreted as a single success metric. The goal result is local recorded-goal reaching, not full-game success.

nuisance_cube.title: Single-run survival across the six nuisance-cube conditions
nuisance_cube.caption: Descriptive final survival percentages over 256 evaluation episodes per cell, with one learned-model/policy run per condition. Global and Grid JEPA policies train in their latent models; Flow pixels and Flow latent denote different policy observation interfaces inside the pixel-generative model. Real CNN trains in the simulator. Center rule is a nonlearned position-feedback baseline, not a learned world model. Imagined-policy training uses 1,228,800 transitions; the real CNN uses 1,499,136 real transitions. The no-wall cube crosses no noise, frame-wise gray noise and episode-fixed gray noise with still or wind dynamics. A state-blind alternating policy achieves 100% survival in the archived edge-start checks of all three still conditions (runs/stoch/*still/baselines_edge.json). Thus survival alone cannot certify use of visual feedback. These single-run cells support a sensitivity audit, not model-family rankings with training-seed uncertainty. The color scale is fixed from 0% to 100%.

readout_by_seed.title: Frozen-latent position readout under gray visual noise and wind
readout_by_seed.caption: Held-out L1 position error of the trained probe on true-observation latents for three independently trained 512-dimensional grid JEPA seeds per condition. Every model uses the same 500,000-transition data-size and 8,500-update training schedule. Gray noise is redrawn per frame or fixed within each episode, crossed with still or hidden-wind dynamics. Each point is a model-seed result; horizontal bars and labels show the three-model means. Results are taken only from the allarms/bench.json benchmark family. This is a failure of the tested readout, not proof of information-theoretic loss. The failing frame-noise plus wind condition does not have near-zero prediction loss, so it must not be presented as an empirical zero-loss optimum.
